description: Machine-readable catalogue of every Intune-WUO finding id. Source of truth for the MCP server and the AI-agent skill. Kept in sync with src/IntuneWUO/Public/Events.ps1 by a Pester test.

autoFixCategories.None: Report only. Intune-WUO never changes this.
autoFixCategories.Services: Controlled by the FixServices switch (service repair, task re-registration).
autoFixCategories.ResetStack: Controlled by the FixResetStack switch (off by default: the reset wipes the Windows Update history list).
autoFixCategories.Updates: Controlled by the InstallOverdueUpdates switch (on in the standalone Remediations package) or by Mode RemediateAndFallback.
autoFixCategories.PolicyKeys: Controlled by the FixPolicyKeys switch. Not active yet: policy values are not attributed to domain GPO vs local policy, so nothing is removed automatically.

findings.title: DoNotConnectToWindowsUpdateInternetLocations is set
findings.cause: A Group Policy, local policy or stray registry write under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate blocks the device from reaching Windows Update. Windows Autopatch flags this value.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Find the source (gpresult /h, RSOP, ConfigMgr client settings, imaging scripts) and remove it there. On Windows 11 24H2 builds with KB5101684 (26100.8973 and later) deploy the Intune policy Update/IgnoreWindowsUpdateGroupPolicies = 1 so Windows ignores Windows Update Group Policy.

findings.title: DisableWindowsUpdateAccess is set
findings.cause: Policy removes access to Windows Update features. Windows Autopatch flags this value.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Remove the source policy, or deploy IgnoreWindowsUpdateGroupPolicies = 1 where supported.

findings.title: AU\NoAutoUpdate is set
findings.cause: Automatic Updates is switched off by policy. Windows Autopatch flags this value.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Remove the source policy, or deploy IgnoreWindowsUpdateGroupPolicies = 1 where supported.

findings.title: An intranet update service (WSUS) is configured
findings.cause: UseWUServer, WUServer or UpdateServiceUrl is present, so the device may scan a WSUS server instead of Windows Update.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Remove the WSUS configuration at its source, or set the SetPolicyDrivenUpdateSourceFor* policies to 0 (Windows Update). The default for those policies is 1 (WSUS).

findings.title: WSUS configured and DisableDualScan is on
findings.cause: With a WSUS URL, DisableDualScan stops the device scanning Windows Update, which blocks Autopatch-managed updates.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Do not configure UpdateServiceUrl/UpdateServiceUrlAlternate, or set SetPolicyDrivenUpdateSourceFor<type> to 0 for the relevant update types.

findings.title: Windows Update service (wuauserv) is disabled
findings.cause: The service start type is Disabled (a stopped trigger-start service is healthy and is not flagged).
findings.toolAction: Sets the start type back to Manual (its default) when Mode is Remediate or RemediateAndFallback and FixServices = 1.
findings.adminAction: If it keeps being disabled (the tool suppresses the fix after FixMaxRepeats), find what disables it: security baselines, hardening scripts, third-party tools.

findings.title: Update Orchestrator service (UsoSvc) is disabled
findings.cause: The service start type is Disabled.
findings.toolAction: Sets the start type to Automatic and starts it.
findings.adminAction: Find what disables it (security baselines, hardening scripts).

findings.title: Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) is disabled
findings.cause: The service start type is Disabled.
findings.toolAction: Sets the start type to Manual.
findings.adminAction: Find what disables it.

findings.title: Windows Update Medic Service (WaaSMedicSvc) is disabled
findings.cause: The service start type is Disabled.
findings.toolAction: Attempts to set Manual. Windows protects this service, so the attempt is expected to fail and is reported as a failed fix.
findings.adminAction: Investigate manually; usually caused by third-party 'update blocker' tools.

findings.title: Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant (wlidsvc) is disabled
findings.cause: Required by Windows Autopatch and the Windows Update for Business deployment service. If it is Disabled the device cannot receive Autopatch-managed updates.
findings.toolAction: Sets the start type to Manual (default, trigger-start).
findings.adminAction: Find what disables it (often a hardening baseline) and exempt it.

findings.title: Connected User Experiences and Telemetry (DiagTrack) is disabled
findings.cause: Diagnostic data cannot be sent, which Autopatch reporting needs.
findings.toolAction: Sets the start type to Automatic and starts it.
findings.adminAction: Review privacy/hardening baselines that disable it.

findings.title: Quality updates are paused by the user, not by policy
findings.cause: PausedQualityStatus is set but no Intune policy pause exists.
findings.toolAction: Removes the user-pause values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings when FixPauses = 1.
findings.adminAction: Deploy SetDisablePauseUXAccess = 1 in the update ring so users cannot pause.

findings.title: Feature updates are paused by the user, not by policy
findings.cause: PausedFeatureStatus is set but no Intune policy pause exists.
findings.toolAction: Removes the user feature-pause values when FixPauses = 1.
findings.adminAction: Deploy SetDisablePauseUXAccess = 1.

findings.title: Updates are paused by Intune policy
findings.cause: A pause was deliberately set by policy (PauseQualityUpdates / PauseQualityUpdatesStartTime).
findings.toolAction: Never changed.
findings.adminAction: None unless the pause was not intended; policy pauses last 35 days from the start date.

findings.title: Diagnostic data is below Required
findings.cause: AllowTelemetry is 0. Windows Autopatch needs Required (1) or higher.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Deploy System/AllowTelemetry = 1 (Required) or higher through Intune.

findings.title: The last MDM sync is older than SyncStaleHours
findings.cause: The device has not checked in with Intune recently (offline, broken enrollment, blocked network).
findings.toolAction: Starts the enrollment's PushLaunch sync task when FixSyncAndCleanup = 1.
findings.adminAction: If it stays stale, check network access to Intune endpoints and the enrollment health.

findings.title: No successful Windows Update scan within ScanStaleDays
findings.cause: The Windows Update stack is probably broken or blocked.
findings.toolAction: Resets the update components (renames SoftwareDistribution and catroot2), at most once per ResetCooldownDays and never during an install or with a restart pending. SIDE EFFECT: this also resets the Windows Update history list shown in Settings (installed updates stay installed). Only the newest backup folder is kept. Runs only when FixResetStack = 1 (off by default).
findings.adminAction: If scans still fail after a reset, check proxy/TLS inspection and WSUS leftovers.

findings.title: Free disk space is below MinFreeDiskGB
findings.cause: Updates need free space to download and install.
findings.toolAction: Deletes temp files older than 7 days and runs DISM component cleanup (20-minute cap) when FixSyncAndCleanup = 1.
findings.adminAction: If still low, free space or reimage; also blocks the fallback installer.

findings.title: A restart is pending
findings.cause: A servicing or Windows Update restart is waiting.
findings.toolAction: Reports only. Intune-WUO never restarts a device.
findings.adminAction: Restarts follow the ring deadline and grace period. Consider native maintenance windows.

findings.title: ConfigMgr client present
findings.cause: A co-managed device may still have Windows Update owned by ConfigMgr.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Move the Windows Update policies and Device configuration co-management workloads to Intune and clear ConfigMgr client Software Updates settings.

findings.title: Windows Autopatch device readiness failed
findings.cause: The Autopatch Client Broker's latest RunDeviceReadinessChecks has a non-zero ResultsBitmask or error codes.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Review the Autopatch Devices blade (Not ready) and Autopatch alerts for the reason.

findings.title: Autopatch readiness has not been reported for over 7 days
findings.cause: The Client Broker is not running its checks or cannot reach the service.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Check the Windows Autopatch Client Broker app status and ClientBroker.log.

findings.title: Windows Autopatch Client Broker is not installed
findings.cause: The optional broker is missing, so Autopatch's on-device readiness result is unavailable.
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Install it from Intune admin center > Tenant administration > Windows Autopatch > Tenant management > Manage client broker.

findings.title: The fallback scheduled task is missing or disabled
findings.cause: Mode is RemediateAndFallback but \IntuneWUO\IntuneWUO-Fallback is not registered or is disabled.
findings.toolAction: Re-registers the task from the installed package.
findings.adminAction: If it keeps disappearing, check the Win32 app assignment and anything removing scheduled tasks.

findings.title: Hotpatch enrolled but the OS is too old
findings.cause: Hotpatch needs Windows 11 24H2 (build 26100) or later. Reported only when hotpatch enrollment is known (enrollment detection is not implemented yet).
findings.toolAction: Reports only.
findings.adminAction: Upgrade the device or exclude it from the hotpatch policy.

findings.title: Hotpatch needs virtualization-based security running
findings.cause: VBS is not running on a hotpatch-enrolled device.
findings.toolAction: Reports only. Never changes VBS.
findings.adminAction: Deploy the Intune policy VirtualizationBasedTechnology (VBS), then restart.

findings.title: Arm64 hotpatch needs CHPE disabled
findings.cause: HotPatchRestrictions is not 1 on an Arm64 hotpatch-enrolled device.
findings.toolAction: Reports only. Never changes CHPE.
findings.adminAction: Deploy the Intune DisableCHPE policy (System/DisableCHPE) and restart. Note that this can affect 32-bit x86 apps on Arm.

findings.title: An approved quality update is overdue
findings.cause: Windows Update has offered a quality or security update (so Autopatch approved it) for longer than the ring deadline (ConfigureDeadlineForQualityUpdates, default 7) plus FallbackGraceDays, counted from its release date plus the ring deferral (DeferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays), and it is still not installed.
findings.toolAction: Installs exactly the overdue offered updates through the native Windows Update API (default service, no drivers, no feature updates), never restarts, and stops after FallbackMaxAttempts failures. Skipped when a restart is pending, disk is low, an install is running, the device is on battery or native maintenance windows are configured.
findings.adminAction: If it keeps failing, read the HResult in the IntuneWUO log and Get-WindowsUpdateLog; check disk space, proxy/TLS inspection and the Autopatch release status.
